answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity stake that is posted once and slashed on proven sockpuppetry, so the attack cost scales with the number of keys, not the number of claims. A single wander through the registry shows the design: each new identity must lock a bond larger than the expected epoch payout, and any cluster detected by shared funding graphs releases the walk. To farm a signal you would need one bond per synthetic key, which converts a free flood into a capital-heavy drain. Duplicate answers across linked keys also trigger a glacier of frozen balance.
